title: A Small Network and Its Gradient: One Hidden Layer, Backpropagation Written Out, and a Check by Finite Differences

questions.question: What happens when a network is trained with a gradient that has a mistake in it?
options: It crashes at the first step
Training runs, and the error falls little or not at all, with nothing saying why
The compiler refuses the code
The weights become NaN at once
questions.explanation: A wrong gradient is a direction that is not downhill. Nothing in the arithmetic notices, which is why it must be checked.

questions.question: How many weights does a network with 8 hidden units, two inputs and one output have?
options: Twice 8
One per sample
questions.explanation: Two input weights and a bias per unit, an output weight per unit, and one output bias: 4 times 8 plus 1.

questions.question: What did the finite difference check find, for the right gradient and for one with 1 - tanh squared left out?
options: 0.123, and less than one part in a million
Both about 0.123
Zero both times
Less than one part in a million, and 0.123
questions.explanation: The right gradient agreed to better than one part in a million; the slip was off by 0.123, far beyond what rounding explains.

questions.question: What is the gradient of the output bias, for one sample?
options: The output itself
The target
The error, output less target
Zero
questions.explanation: The bias adds to the output directly, so the derivative of half the squared error is the error.

questions.question: Why must the starting weights not all be equal?
options: Units that start the same get the same gradient and stay the same, so the layer acts as one unit
Equal weights cannot be stored
tanh of equal numbers is zero
The seed requires them to differ
questions.explanation: Symmetry is never broken by gradient descent, so random starting weights are needed.

questions.question: Why is the finite difference check a test and not part of training?
options: It is less accurate than backpropagation in every case
It costs two forward passes per weight, where backpropagation gives every weight for about one
It only works for one hidden unit
It changes the weights
questions.explanation: For a network of thousands of weights the check is thousands of times dearer. It is run when the gradient code changes.
